title: Immunoblot Assay for Densitometric Determination of Ubiquitin Forms in Drosophila
author: Ágota agy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s5teg6n
materials: Use the Gel Analysis tool of the ImageJ 1.49v software (NIH, Bethesda, Maryland) to determine the density of the bands corresponding to the monoubiquitin and ubiquitin standards. Copy the band intensity data to an excel table for subsequent statistical analysis. https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/index.html

steps.title: Collect Drosophila tissue
steps.instruction: Collect 5–6 mg of synchronized Drosophila melanogaster animals or tissues into pre‑chilled 1.5 mL micro‑fuge tubes.

steps.title: Add buffers and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL buffer F (preserves conjugated ubiquitins) and 100 µL buffer T (converts conjugated ubiquitins to monomers) to each sample and homogenize with a plastic tissue grinder.

steps.title: Clarify extracts by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenates at 4 °C, 13 000 RCF for 10 min. Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge again at 4 °C, 13 000 RCF for 10 min, and transfer the second supernatant to another fresh 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Determine protein in buffer F
steps.instruction: Use 1 µL of the buffer F extract to measure total protein concentration.

steps.title: Prepare buffer F samples
steps.instruction: Add 4× Laemmli sample buffer to the buffer F protein extract and boil for 5 min.

steps.title: Incubate buffer T extracts
steps.instruction: Incubate the buffer T protein extracts at 25 °C for 3 h.

steps.title: Determine protein in buffer T
steps.instruction: Use 1 µL of the buffer T extract to measure total protein concentration.

steps.title: Prepare buffer T samples
steps.instruction: Add 4× Laemmli sample buffer to the buffer T protein extract and boil for 5 min.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE with standards
steps.instruction: Prepare a 14 % (w/v) Tris‑Glycine SDS‑PAGE gel, 1 mm thick. Prepare running buffer containing 25 mM Tris (pH 8.3), 192 mM Glycine and 0.1 % SDS. Load 10 µL of appropriately diluted total protein extracts together with ubiquitin standards of 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 pmol. Electrophorese until the dye front reaches the bottom.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to PVDF
steps.instruction: Perform a wet transfer onto a PVDF membrane at a constant 300 mA using transfer buffer containing 20 mM Tris (pH 8.0), 150 mM Glycine and 20 % methanol for 2 h 30 min.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in 5 % non‑fat milk prepared in TBS at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Antibody incubations and washes
steps.instruction: Perform primary and secondary antibody steps with intervening washes.

substeps.instruction: Incubate membrane with anti‑ubiquitin antibody diluted 1:1000 in TBST‑B (TBS + 0.05 % Tween‑20 + 1 % BSA) at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash membrane three times with TBS‑T by vigorous shaking for 10 min total (≈3 min per wash).
Incubate membrane with HRP‑conjugated goat anti‑rabbit secondary antibody diluted 1:30 000 in TBST‑B at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash membrane three times with TBS‑T by vigorous shaking for 10 min total (≈3 min per wash).

steps.title: Develop chemiluminescent signal
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in Immobilon Western Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate for 3 min, then cover the membrane with Saran Wrap™.

steps.title: Expose and develop X‑ray film
steps.instruction: In a dark room place a sheet of X‑ray film over the membrane and expose for 20–30 seconds. Immediately develop the film using Tetenal X‑ray developer and fixative solutions.

steps.title: Digitize film images
steps.instruction: Capture the developed film with a digital camera or a high‑resolution gel documentation system such as the BioDoc‑It™ 220 Imaging System.

steps.title: Quantify ubiquitin via calibration curve
steps.instruction: Measure band intensities of the ubiquitin standards (y) and their known amounts (x). In Microsoft Excel with the XLSTAT add‑on, fit a four‑parameter logistic curve to generate a regression equation, then use this equation to calculate the ubiquitin concentration of the sample of interest.
